function: p. 1, 4: Online selection of incremental IRS phase shifts from a codebook, posed as a contextual bandit, to maximize the sum rate in a time-varying near-field MU-MISO system.
system: p. 3, 12, 13: Passive reflecting IRS (4x8=32 elements), BS with M=8 antennas, single-antenna UEs (L=2 default), near-field TDD MU-MISO, blocked direct path, 28 GHz.
method: p. 10-12: GLinUCB, a linear contextual-bandit (LinUCB-style) reinforcement learner with unitary-matrix contexts on a geodesic metric space; learns online from sum-rate rewards in simulation.
data_channel: p. 3, 12: Self-built near-field spherical-wave LoS plus statistical NLoS cascaded channel at 28 GHz, simulated UE tracks in an urban canyon, 100 Monte Carlo seeds.
test_conditions: p. 12-14: Online learning and evaluation in the same simulated scenario; figures sweep transmit power, IRS elements, IRS count, UEs and blocks per episode; no cross-scenario test reported.
baselines: p. 12-13: Random action selection (RAN), UCB, KernelUCB [37], DQN with ResNet [38], Transformer DQN (DTQN) [39]; the MAX curve is the theoretical optimum.
metrics: p. 12-13: Average sum rate, cumulative reward and regret, episodes to reach 95% of the maximum sum rate, and single-step training time.
complexity: p. 12: Linear complexity O(NF L^2), at most cubic in the number of features; p. 13: DQN single-step training time about 74 times longer.
openness: none; no code or data link in the paper, the simulated dataset is described but not released (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 12: "to derive simulated near-field channel data"; the channel is the paper's own spherical-wave LoS plus statistical NLoS model (p. 3), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "Fig. 7 displays the average performance of all algorithms as the number of IRS elements gradually increases"; sweeps are separate online runs, and no transfer, fine-tuning or unseen-scenario test is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "The baseline algorithms used in this paper include UCB algorithm and DQN [38] algorithm"; random action selection (RAN) is the non-learned baseline; sum rate compared in Figs. 5-10.
q4_support: p. 12: "we have linear complexity as O(NF L2 )"; p. 13 also reports a DQN training time about 74 times longer than the proposed algorithm.
q5_support: p. 12: "the multiple-step MU generated by simulation is saved as a dataset for offline training"; the dataset is self-generated, and no code or data link and no public dataset appear.
notes: Include, area 3: GLinUCB is an online reinforcement-learning (contextual bandit) controller whose learned coefficients choose the IRS phase-shift increment (abstract p. 1; Algorithm 1 p. 12), so the learned element performs RIS configuration. The BS has 8 antennas and there is a RIS, so the system rule does not apply. Results are sum-rate curves (pp. 13-14). q3 is met: RAN is the random non-learned configuration, DQN [38] is an earlier learned IRS method, and UCB, KernelUCB and DTQN are standard learners on the same problem. q2 is not met: the sweeps over UEs, IRS elements and IRS count are separate online runs, and p. 14 itself notes limited generalization. q1: custom simulator, with the LoS model taken from reference [24], not from 3GPP.
